blocks.text: Adaptive Traffic Steering in Private Access (ZPA) is a dynamic rerouting feature designed to maintain application availability and minimize service disruptions during network degradation. It addresses performance issues such as slow response times and connection timeouts caused by transient conditions, including packet loss and increased application round-trip time. By using real-time network health metrics, Adaptive Traffic Steering automatically redirects traffic to alternate paths when degradation is detected, reducing the need for manual failover interventions.

Adaptive Traffic Steering ensures that application efficiency and uptime are preserved across both pinpointed and extensive infrastructure failures. It serves to mitigate the consequences of various network disruptions, such as:

blocks.item: Regional access failures, including wars or environmental disasters

blocks.text: Adaptive Traffic Steering is only available for organizations that have Business Continuity configured. To learn more, see Understanding Business Continuity.

blocks.heading: Adaptive Traffic Steering for Application Segments

blocks.text: When you configure a defined application segment, Adaptive Traffic Steering can be enabled to prioritize mission-critical applications and dynamically route traffic along healthier paths.
When you enable Adaptive Traffic Steering for applications segments, a warning message appears alerting you that alternate routing paths can introduce higher latency compared to direct connections.
